findings.checklist_item: Correct Correction #2's provenance: cite B6 of epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc (not story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c) as the owner of the .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ HEAD removal, and reconcile 'retained in history' with the cited session log's 'sitting in the tree AT HEAD.'
evidence: show_ticket 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c: title 'A4-3: verify the landed call-site suppression; no differ change required', file_impact_scope 'none', file_impact []; no_file_impact_reason ties it to A4-1 differ call-site suppression — nothing about .bridge_state.bak-retarget/

Epic 0303 scope + epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc child list: 'B6 delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget (33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree at HEAD)'; '(6) .bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json is 33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree AT HEAD - delete before the strip' (session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 [3/3])
Contradiction: plan says '33 MB retained in history' (i.e., not at HEAD) but the cited session log says 'sitting in the tree AT HEAD'
findings.finding: Correction #2 misattributes the removal of the .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ prefix to story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c and mischaracterizes where the 33 MB lives. Ticket 4804 is 'A4-3: verify the landed call-site suppression' with file_impact_scope=none / empty file_impact — it does not touch .bridge_state.bak-retarget/. The real HEAD removal is owned by B6 of epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc. The plan also calls the 33 MB 'retained in history' while its own cited session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 and epic 42eb/B6 both state the .bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json blob is 'sitting in the tree AT HEAD.'
findings.location: Required corrections — item 2 ('Strip both .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ prefixes — story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c removes the latter at HEAD only; session log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 records the measured 33 MB retained in history.')
scenarios: A reader/implementer trusts the stated provenance, looks to 4804/A4-3 to confirm the HEAD state of .bridge_state.bak-retarget/, finds no such change, and cannot reconcile the correction's justification
If B6 (the actual HEAD-removal owner) is assumed already landed based on the wrong citation, the strip could run before .bak-retarget/ is gone at HEAD, altering the expected tree-identity assumptions
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the citation with: 'B6 (epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc) deletes .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ at HEAD (33,025,572 bytes); session log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 records that this blob sits in the tree AT HEAD and across history, so the strip must remove the prefix from all revisions.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct correction-2's citation from 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c to the actual .bak-retarget remover (B6 in epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc) and state that B6 must have landed at the recorded old tip before the strip runs.
evidence: Plan: 'Strip both .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ prefixes — story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c removes the latter at HEAD only'
Ticket 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c title/desc: 'A4-3 ... no new code ... This story closes by verifying the landed call-site behavior', file_impact_scope 'none'
Epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc scope: 'B6 delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget (33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree at HEAD)' and 'B6 must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim'
findings.finding: Correction 2 mis-attributes the removal of .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ at HEAD to story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c, but that story ('A4-3: verify the landed call-site suppression; no differ change required') has file_impact=none and never touches .bak-retarget/. The actual remover is B6 in epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc, whose AC is '.bridge_state.bak-retarget is absent from the tree at HEAD' and which the epic marks as a hard prerequisite ('B6 must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim so the strip does not retain those blobs').
scenarios: An implementer follows the citation to 4804 to confirm .bak-retarget is gone at the old tip, finds a no-op verification story, and cannot establish the precondition the strip depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'story 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c removes the latter at HEAD only' with a reference to B6 (epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc), and note the dry-run must assert .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ is already absent at the recorded old tip before stripping.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep -v` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC2 explicit that the compared old-tip tree must already have .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ removed (post-B6), so that stripping both prefixes but re-adding only .bridge_state/ yields a byte-identical tree.
evidence: Plan AC: 'rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree} equals the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add ... not one byte of live content changed'
Plan correction 3: 'Derive the re-add set DYNAMICALLY — git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/' (re-adds only .bridge_state/)
session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 blocker (4): '.bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json is 33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree AT HEAD - delete before the strip'
findings.finding: AC2's tree-identity invariant ('rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree} equals the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add') is not self-consistent as stated with correction 2 + correction 3: the strip removes BOTH .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ from all history, but the dynamic re-add (ls-tree ... -- .bridge_state/) restores ONLY .bridge_state/. This only yields tree-equality if the recorded old-tip tree contains NO .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ entry. The plan never states this precondition, and the session log records the .bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json as still present at HEAD unless deleted first.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, second bullet (tree-identity) + Required corrections items 2 and 3
scenarios: If the old tip used for the tree comparison still carries .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ (B6 not yet landed / wrong old-tip captured), the stripped-and-re-added tree omits that subtree and AC2 fails or, worse, the assertion is silently satisfied against a post-deletion tree the plan never defined.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the dry-run first asserts `git ls-tree <old-tip> -- .bridge_state.bak-retarget/` is empty, then compares <new-tip>^{tree} against that old-tip tree; document that the invariant presupposes B6 landed at the recorded old tip.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that A6-1 must record/retain a backup ref (e.g. refs/backup/tickets-pre-strip = old-tip) before the force-with-lease push, as the explicit back-out path for the irreversible rewrite.
evidence: 'publish with --force-with-lease, never --force. A lease failure means the remote moved; abort without publication'
force-with-lease only detects concurrent remote movement; it is not a rollback path for an already-published irreversible history rewrite
findings.finding: The Publication constraint section specifies --force-with-lease and abort-on-lease-failure (which guards only against the remote having moved), but names no post-push back-out mechanism such as retaining a backup ref of the pre-rewrite tip. The tree-identity assertion proves content equality before push, so a bad rewrite is caught pre-push; however, once the force-push lands, consumers on the old history have no documented recovery ref if the published rewrite must be reverted.
findings.location: Publication constraint (owned by A6-1, not this script)
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Publication constraint note: before pushing, tag/push a backup ref of the pre-rewrite tip so the old history is restorable if the rewrite must be reverted post-publication.

findings.finding: Correction #2 (strip `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` from history) has no dedicated acceptance criterion verifying it was actually stripped. AC #2 (tree identity) cannot catch this omission because `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` files do not exist at HEAD. AC #4 (pack size ≤15%) may still pass even if the 33 MB bak-retarget history is left intact.
findings.location: Required Corrections #2 vs Acceptance Criteria section
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'After rewrite, `git log --all --oneline -- .bridge_state.bak-retarget/` returns zero commits. Tier: repo-level assertion in the dry-run harness.'

findings.finding: The leaf's pack-size AC uses a percentage threshold (<=15% of original) that is less stringent than the parent epic's absolute ceiling (<=150 MB). On the measured original of 1,172,586,762 bytes, 15% ≈ 176 MB — a script that passes the leaf's AC4 could still fail the parent's AC ('A fresh unfiltered clone of tickets is <=150 MB').
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4 ('Pack size drops to <=15% of the original')
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC4 with: 'Pack size of a fresh unfiltered clone drops to **<=150 MB** (the parent epic's committed ceiling). Tier: repo-level measurement.' This is strictly tighter than the current 15% and is directly derivable from the parent's AC.
